subject: Clarify PII tokenization, cross-border data flow & KMS mapping for DPA
messages:
From: Emily Rhodes <emily@healthgrid.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealthGrid Contracts <contracts@healthgrid.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on PII handling, tokenization & cross-border during DPA review

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending the draft DPA earlier. Before we loop in our security team for a full audit, can you help clarify a few technical points so we can scope their review? High-level asks below — simple yes/no plus short details would be great.

1) Tokenization at rest: Does Redwood offer optional tokenization/pseudonymization of raw PII at rest or only encryption-at-rest via KMS? If tokenization is supported, where is the token mapping stored and who has access?

2) Cross-border data flow: We need a clear picture of what metadata or PII may traverse outside the US in normal operation (e.g., batched telemetry, analytics, or model telemetry). Does Redwood have a diagram showing which flows may cross regions?

3) KMS mapping: If we use our own customer-managed keys (BYOK), can we map which data blobs/objects are encrypted under the customer key vs Redwood-managed keys? We’ll likely request a table mapping logical artifacts to key ownership.

4) Exemptions & retention: Are there programmatic controls to exempt certain customer records from deletion/retention policies (legal hold or export controls)?

Attachments: please point me at any dataflow diagram and a KMS mapping spreadsheet if available.

Goal: get enough detail to feed our security questionnaire and confirm what evidence we need to request from Redwood.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Rhodes
Sr. InfoSec Program Manager, HealthGrid
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Rhodes <emily@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on PII handling, tokenization & cross-border during DPA review

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below; attaching a diagram and a KMS mapping workbook for your review. If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute tech walkthrough with Monica (product security) and Markus (infra) tomorrow.

1) Tokenization at rest: No built-in application-level tokenization product today — we provide encryption-at-rest using customer-managed KMS (BYOK) or Redwood-managed keys. Customers that require tokenization typically implement tokenization in the ingestion layer before data hits Redwood.

2) Cross-border flows: Normal inference request/response traffic remains in the region configured for your deployment (we honor region pinning in Dedicated/Private). Metadata used for telemetry (e.g., anonymized model latency samples) is optionally aggregated in our central telemetry platform; for customers in a region we can disable cross-region telemetry. See attached redwood_dataflow_v2.pdf for flows and optional telemetry toggles.

3) KMS mapping: Attached kms_key_mapping.xlsx maps logical artifact groups (model checkpoints, audit logs, persisted cache, customer payloads) to key ownership (Customer BYOK vs Redwood-managed). Key point: customer payloads can be encrypted with your key in Dedicated/Private deployments; in Hosted mode, customers can opt into BYOK for sensitive buckets.

4) Exemptions & retention: We expose retention controls per-customer and per-route. Legal hold is supported via an admin API flag for affected datasets; we can lock records from deletion and provide an audit trail. We cannot selectively exempt records from exports driven by regulatory obligations (govt requests) without a formal process.

Attachments: redwood_dataflow_v2.pdf (diagram), kms_key_mapping.xlsx (workbook), soc2-sample-evidence.txt (example logs).

Next steps: I’ll CC our Security PM Monica to confirm the telemetry toggles and Markus to confirm the BYOK constraints. Happy to run the walkthrough — suggest Tue 10am PT.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Questions on PII handling, tokenization & cross-border during DPA review

Hi Emily — quick technical clarifications, expanding on Karthik’s notes.

- Telemetry: By default we collect anonymized telemetry for system health (latency, error rates). For customers who require strict data residency we provide a telemetry opt-out which prevents any request-level metadata from leaving region. Opt-out is a boolean flag at the tenant level.

- Tokenization: Customers that need tokenization at the platform layer generally deploy a pre-ingest transform (lambda or sidecar) which replaces PII with tokens before sending requests. We have internal patterns and sample code (we can share a short repo).

- KMS/BYOK: Technical constraints: BYOK requires a customer-managed key in a cloud KMS with cross-account/granting configured to allow our runtime to use the key for encrypt/decrypt operations. For on-prem/private deployments we can integrate with vault/HSM (requires ops coordination). The mapping sheet shows which artifacts may be encrypted under BYOK — note that ephemeral caches used for KV acceleration may still be encrypted with a runtime key and are not always bound to BYOK depending on hosting mode.

- Audit logs & evidence: We can provide a scoped SOC2 evidence bundle (sample) and specific logs for key usage, access events, and admin actions. For production audits we typically provide a combination of screenshots, signed statements, and CSV exports.

I’ll be on the walkthrough Tuesday 10am PT and can demo the telemetry toggle and point you to the sample repo.

Best,
Monica Patel
Product Security Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi all — short technical answer on key rotation and historical decryptability.

- For cloud-provider BYOK: If the customer keeps previous key versions / key material (i.e., they do not schedule automatic irreversible deletion of old keys), objects encrypted with prior key versions remain decryptable. Rotation in most managed KMS is implemented as new key versions under the same key resource; we use the KMS API to reference the correct version when decrypting. If a customer purges old key versions, those historical objects become unrecoverable.

- For HSM/Vault: Behavior depends on the vault config; we need an ops runbook for the integration.

Action: I’ll annotate the kms_key_mapping.xlsx with a column about rotation impact and add a short note in the redwood_dataflow_v2.pdf referencing the telemetry opt-out. Attaching both updated files to the walkthrough calendar invite.

-Markus
